title: ICE LAB: CONTROL THE SLIP
subtitle: Drive onto a low-grip ice lane and observe how measured slip changes the command envelope.
briefing: The ice lane is a physical low-friction surface, not a hidden ROBOT input.
Use the measured wheel, IMU, LiDAR, and contact response to keep the stop safe.
A failed run remains useful evidence when the physical limit is reproducible.

prediction.question: What should change when the robot enters the ice lane?

choices.label: Measured slip reduces speed demand while safety stays active
choices.explanation: The ROBOT uses sensor residuals and keeps its footprint and validator contract unchanged.

choices.label: Read the SIM friction coefficient directly
choices.explanation: Material parameters belong to SIM and never cross into ROBOT.

choices.label: Increase wheel demand until the route is forced
choices.explanation: More command cannot make a low-grip contact envelope safe.

running_prompt: Compare ROBOT estimate, slip evidence, local safety, and physical contact in Engineering view.

lessons: Surface friction is a plant property; the robot infers traction from measurements.
The same validator, Safety gate, and watchdog apply on ice and dry ground.
A safe controller reports a physical limit instead of hiding it with a truth hint.
